refuted.problem: Check 5 (dimensional legitimacy) fails. The raw text is "Take 3 to 6 grams daily with water or as directed by the Vaidya." That is a DAILY TOTAL, not an amount per dose. The formulary figure (AFI Part I 7:34, "1 to 3 g") is a per-dose weight. The claim presents 3 to 6 g as Maharishi's adult dose and compares it per-dose against 1 to 3 g, which is a per-day vs per-dose mismatch; the label gives no frequency, so the per-dose amount cannot be derived. Digits and quote are otherwise verbatim and correct, and the relation would also only touch the formulary range at the single point 3 g.
refuted.correction: Report as "3 to 6 g per day (frequency unstated)" and either exclude it from the per-dose comparison or label the relation as not directly comparable to the AFI per-dose figure.

refuted.problem: Relation 'overlapping' overstates the arithmetic. Label range is 1 to 3 g (digits verified, quote verbatim, adult/unstated, dimensionally fine), formulary is 3 to 6 g. The two ranges share only the single endpoint 3 g; every other label value lies below the formulary minimum. Calling that 'overlapping' implies a shared span that does not exist.
refuted.correction: Keep the numbers (1 to 3 g) but relabel the relation as 'below the formulary range, meeting it only at 3 g' (or whatever the vocabulary's below/touching term is), not 'overlapping'.

refuted.problem: The file holds two Maharishi Ayurveda labels, not one. The 50 ml page says "Take 3 to 12 ml Twice a day" (the quoted text is verbatim and the digits are right), but the second page (maharishiayurvedaindia.com/products/saraswatarishta) says "1-2 teaspoon daily after meals", i.e. roughly 5 to 10 ml once a day, which is entirely lower than the formulary 12 to 24 ml. The claim publishes 3 to 12 ml as the brand's figure while the brand's own other page contradicts it on both amount and frequency. Also, 3 to 12 ml meets 12 to 24 ml only at the single boundary point 12, so "overlapping" overstates the agreement; 3 to 12 ml is also exactly the range Kerala Ayurveda labels for children, and the Maharishi page states no population.
refuted.correction: Either cite both Maharishi pages ("3 to 12 ml twice a day" on the 50 ml page; "1-2 teaspoon daily" on the other) and describe the relation as touching the formulary range only at 12 ml, or drop Maharishi from the comparison rather than publish one of two inconsistent figures as the manufacturer's dose.
